description: The client has the menu (protocol/02-doors.md, "The client has the menu"): the words between a world in a frame and the page above it that draws the visitor's console. `describing`: what a client keeps of each `world` a framed page sends as `{ nswp: "menu", world }` (`opts.own`: the page is of the client's own origin; `opts.also`: visitor's tabs this client still takes from a world), or null. `counting`: the limits on how much, with what was sent said in words and what was kept as counts. `down`: what a world makes of each word from the page above. `up`: what a client makes of each word from the page in its frame. `here`: the version spoken with a world, from its `here`: the lower of the two, or 0. The rules: a client's settings are cleaned as a link's are, so `filesAnywhere: true` is dropped from them (that switch is turned on only by the visitor's own press on the world's own row) and `false` is taken; one word says one thing, and a word with anything in it that only the other side says is not read; a client may tell a world to sign the visitor out (`sign: "out"`), which carries nothing and can only take away, and there is no word for signing in; `state.signIn` is one of `signIn`, a fact the client words its own row from; nothing is run and every word is text; what is unknown, over a limit or not the world's to say is left out, never cut to fit or mended; in a tab both fill (`tabs.world` has them all; Sound, Help and Moving among them) a client draws its own rows first and the world's below, under the world's name; a line has anything unseen made a space and its ends trimmed; text to copy and text typed are carried whole or not at all; characters are counted as code points, and bytes as the UTF-8 of the JSON without pictures. `cardPicture` is what comes before a tab's id where a picture is for the card at that tab's head, and no row's id may begin with it. No picture is in these examples: JSON has none, and a reader with no check for them keeps none. A press may carry a file the visitor chose (`file`), and a world may hand a picture or a clip up to be saved (`save`); a file is not something this page can hold, so only what is refused for not being one is here, and the rest is in the core's tests.

describing.name: a_whole_description
describing.why: Everything a world may say, kept as said.

describing.name: nothing_said
describing.why: An empty description is a world with no name and no tabs.

describing.name: a_guest_nobody_named
describing.why: `guest` is said of who the world has: where it has nobody (`named` false), it is not taken.

describing.name: not_a_description
describing.why: Text, a list or nothing is no description.

describing.name: the_visitors_own_tabs
describing.why: A world never fills the visitor's own tabs: each is left out whole.

describing.name: a_tab_the_client_still_takes
describing.why: A client that doesn't yet run Following itself takes it from a world (`also`), and a row may be typed into there.

describing.name: the_clients_own_page
describing.why: A page of the client's own origin may fill any tab, and add more than two of its own.

describing.name: sound_and_help
describing.why: Sound and Help are filled by both. A world adds what is its own to them (the piece it is playing; a note about itself), which a client draws below its own rows, under the world's name. Nothing typed goes to a world from either: a `field` row there is left out.

sections.note: Six sculptures, each a few lines of code turned into a shape.
Six sculptures, each a few lines of code turned into a shape.

describing.name: moving
describing.why: Moving is filled by both. How the visitor moves is the client's to switch; a world adds what it does for them, such as a jump, which a client draws below its own rows under the world's name. Nothing typed goes to a world from Moving.

describing.name: a_help_note_too_long
describing.why: A world's words in Help are a note of at most the limit. One that is over is left out, never cut to fit.

describing.name: three_tabs_of_its_own
describing.why: A world may add two tabs. The third is left out, and so is one with no name.

describing.name: the_clients_names_stand
describing.why: A tab every place has is named by the client: a world's name and icon for it are not taken. A tab said twice is the first.

describing.name: where_a_row_may_be_typed_into
describing.why: A `field` row stands only in the keeper's tab and in a world's own tabs. Elsewhere it is left out.

describing.name: where_a_file_may_be_asked_for
describing.why: A `file` row stands only in Panels and in a world's own tabs, and names the kinds of file it takes from the ones there are (`image`, `video`). A kind that isn't one of those is not taken; a row that names none of them is left out. It is never on the bar: where the file goes is written under it.

describing.name: a_row_that_saves
describing.why: A `save` row is a button whose press may be answered by the world handing a picture or a clip up. It stands wherever a button does, the bar too.

describing.name: rows_left_out
describing.why: A row is left out, never mended: with no id or label, a label over the limit, a kind this doesn't know, a `copy` with no text, a swatch with no colour, an id already said, or an id that begins `card:` (which is how the picture of a tab's card is addressed, and never a row).

describing.name: words_are_text
describing.why: Markup is shown as the letters sent. Anything unseen in a line (a control character, a mark that turns text round) becomes a space, and a line read is trimmed.

describing.name: text_to_copy_is_whole_or_not_at_all
describing.why: Text to copy is kept exactly as written, lines and all, and refused if anything in it is unseen.

describing.name: a_card
describing.why: A card's words are text; the rows it names are that tab's own. Its `proven` mark is dropped: a world's say-so is not the client's to vouch for.

describing.name: a_card_from_the_clients_own_page
describing.why: The proven mark is kept only from a page of the client's own origin, which checked the name itself.

describing.name: state_as_it_can_be
describing.why: What isn't said is not so. With no room nobody is joined; with no headset no session runs; a rule for items this doesn't know is none; and where signing in stands is one of four words, never a world's own sentence.

describing.name: pictures_need_a_check
describing.why: A picture is kept only by a caller that checks it (its kind and size, in a browser). Here there is none.

counting.name: tabs
counting.sent: eighteen tabs: the twelve a world may fill, three of the visitor's own, then three of the world's; 16 are read, so the world's second and third are past the limit

counting.name: too_big
counting.sent: two hundred rows, each with 2000 characters to copy
